title: Measure Costs Right: Make the Right Decisions (Robin Cooper and Robert S. Kaplan, September 1988)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Managers in multi-product firms make pricing, product-mix and technology decisions on distorted cost data, and usually find out only after profits and competitiveness have fallen; the authors argue for more accurate product costing (the article that launched activity-based costing).

title: Time-Driven Activity-Based Costing (Robert S. Kaplan and Steven R. Anderson, November 2004)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Many large activity-based costing projects were abandoned because of cost and staff frustration; the revised approach relies on managers' estimates instead of employee time surveys and gives a more flexible cost model.

title: GMAP 2.0: Revised guidance for a rapidly changing world (31 January 2024)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The second edition of the Global Management Accounting Principles (AICPA & CIMA, June 2023) has four principles: communication influences and creates impact; information is relevant; analysis generates sustainable value; stewardship builds trust.

title: Principles of Accounting, Volume 2: Managerial Accounting, 3.1 Explain Contribution Margin (Franklin, Graybeal and Cooper, 2019)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Contribution margin per unit is price minus variable cost per unit; total contribution margin is sales minus total variable costs; the contribution margin ratio is contribution per unit divided by price. Free textbook under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

title: Principles of Accounting, Volume 2: Managerial Accounting, 4.6 Determine and Dispose of Underapplied or Overapplied Overhead
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Overhead is applied to jobs with a predetermined rate (for example per direct labour hour); the gap between overhead actually incurred and overhead applied is under-applied (debit balance) or over-applied (credit balance) overhead.

title: Principles of Accounting, Volume 2: Managerial Accounting, 7.4 Prepare Flexible Budgets
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A flexible budget restates budgeted costs at the actual level of activity, with variable costs moving and fixed costs staying put; comparing actuals with a static budget can mislead when volume differs from plan.

title: Principles of Accounting, Volume 2: Managerial Accounting, 8.3 Compute and Evaluate Labor Variances
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Labour rate variance = (actual rate - standard rate) x actual hours; labour time (efficiency) variance = (actual hours - standard hours for actual output) x standard rate; the two add to the total labour variance; favourable and unfavourable defined.

title: Principles of Accounting, Volume 2: Managerial Accounting, 10.1 Identify Relevant Information for Decision-Making
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Relevant costs are future costs that differ between options; sunk costs are ignored; in the short run only avoidable costs matter; opportunity cost is the benefit given up by not choosing the other option.

title: Fraud Risk Management Guide, Executive Summary (September 2016)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (PDF text extracted). The 2013 COSO Internal Control framework has 17 principles under five components; principle 8 is considering the potential for fraud when assessing risks; smaller and owner-managed organisations without boards can adapt the guide.

title: Occupational Fraud 2026: A Report to the Nations (press release, 12 May 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 2,402 cases in 143 countries; organisations estimated to lose 5% of revenue a year to fraud; median loss $104,000; median 12 months before detection; 43% detected by tips; smaller businesses had the highest median losses of any size group.

title: IAS 2 Inventories
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Inventory cost includes purchase costs, conversion costs (direct labour and production overhead) and other costs to bring items to their present location and condition; measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value; FIFO or weighted average for interchangeable items, specific identification otherwise.

title: IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Five-step model; revenue recognised over time (typically services) using a measure of progress, or at a point in time (typically goods); effective for periods from 1 January 2018; issued in May 2014 alongside FASB Topic 606.

title: IFRS 18 Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Applies to annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027; new defined subtotals (operating profit; profit before financing and income taxes); disclosure of management-defined performance measures used in public communications.

title: FRS 102 Explainer: a summary of the Periodic Review 2024 changes for financial statements users (30 June 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Most amendments apply to periods beginning on or after 1 January 2026; lessees bring most leases onto the balance sheet (short-term and low-value exemptions); rent expense falls while depreciation and interest rise; gearing, interest cover, current ratio and EBITDA may change; single five-step revenue model; comparatives not always restated.

title: Summary: G702-1992, Application and Certificate for Payment
publisher: AIA Contract Documents (American Institute of Architects)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. G702 is the contractor's payment application and the architect's certificate; it shows contract sum to date, completed and stored work, previous payments, change orders, retainage and the current payment due; it is used with the G703 continuation sheet, which breaks the contract sum down by a contractor-prepared schedule of values.

title: Commercial Payments Bill: overview (19 May 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Bill introduced to Parliament in May 2026, not yet law; maximum payment terms of 60 days with limited exemptions; statutory interest at 8% above Bank of England base rate; deduction and withholding of retention payments under construction contracts to be prohibited, with timing subject to further consultation; lead-in and transition periods; not retrospective.

title: Late payment (Your Europe, last checked 5 August 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. EU B2B and public-authority late payment rules: with no agreed term, interest runs from 30 days after the invoice is received; flat EUR 40 compensation per late invoice plus reasonable recovery costs; statutory rates for 1 July to 31 December 2026 vary by country (for example Germany 10.52%, France 12.40%).

title: Instructions for Form 990 (2025), Part IX Statement of Functional Expenses
supports: Opened with WebFetch (Part IX read at offset 330,000). Expenses split into program services, management and general, and fundraising; where the accounting system does not allocate, any reasonable method may be used and must be documented; example of allocating salary by share of time spent.

title: Changes to charity accounting and reporting (published 31 October 2025)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The updated Charities SORP applies to reporting periods starting on or after 1 January 2026; three tiers by income (up to 500,000 pounds; 500,000 pounds to 15 million pounds; over 15 million pounds); new rules for income and leases; refreshed trustees' report guidance on reserves and plans.

title: The Nonprofit Starvation Cycle (Ann Goggins Gregory and Don Howard, Fall 2009)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Funders' unrealistic overhead expectations lead nonprofits to underspend on and under-report infrastructure; four youth-serving nonprofits reported overhead of 13% to 22% while their actual rates were 17% to 35%.

title: SPI Research publishes its 19th annual Professional Services Maturity Benchmark report (24 February 2026)
publisher: SPI Research (press release via EIN Presswire)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Survey of 509 professional services organisations (2025 data, over 245,000 employees); average billable utilisation 66.4%, the lowest in the study's 19 years; revenue growth 5.2%; headcount growth 2.8%. The full report is paid, so only press-release figures are used.

title: Metric of the Month: Cycle Time for Monthly Close (Perry D. Wiggins, 5 March 2018)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. APQC Open Standards Benchmarking, 2,300 organisations: median 6.4 calendar days from running the trial balance to completed consolidated statements; top 25% 4.8 days or less; bottom 25% 10 or more days.

title: Profit reports
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Profit is reported only for items with a cost recorded when sold; gross profit reports use cost per item; profit margin by order also counts shipping, duties and import taxes; the page does not mention payment or other fees.

title: xero-mcp-server
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Read tools for profit and loss, trial balance, balance sheet, aged receivables and payables, and tracking categories; write tools include creating and updating tracking categories; connections created from 29 April 2026 use granular (V2) scopes, with read-only report scopes listed.

title: quickbooks-online-mcp-server
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 145 tools over 29 entity types plus 11 reports (balance sheet, profit and loss, cash flow, trial balance, general ledger, aged receivables and payables and others); Class and Department supported; OAuth 2.0; write, update and delete tools can be switched off by settings; sandbox recommended for testing.

title: Frequently asked questions about Agent Mode in Excel
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Copilot in Excel has Edit (changes the workbook), Plan (proposes before editing) and Chat (no changes) modes; it can make mistakes and output must be reviewed; Microsoft advises avoiding it for decisions in sensitive areas such as finance; saved changes are visible to co-authors.

title: The Institute of Cost Accountants of India
supports: Opened with WebFetch. India's professional body for cost and management accountants. Listed as the source to check in India; no detail given in the kit.

title: Financial Reporting & Assurance Standards Canada
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Umbrella for Canada's standard-setting boards; covers IFRS Accounting Standards, ASPE (private enterprises) and ASNPO (not-for-profits). Listed as a source to check in Canada; no detail given in the kit.

title: Keeping records (modified 30 June 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Official Canadian page on which business records to keep, in what format and for how long. Listed as a source to check in Canada; no detail given in the kit.
